sections.heading: Is JustMarkets Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Thirteen years of continuous operation, five regulatory licences, 160+ countries served, and a Pro account that charges 0.1 pips with zero commission — on paper, JustMarkets looks like a broker that punches above its weight class. The formerly-named JustForex rebranded in 2022 and picked up a CySEC licence that gives it legitimate EU standing. That Pro account pricing at $1 all-in per lot on EUR/USD is not a typo — it genuinely undercuts brokers like IC Markets ($7 all-in) and Pepperstone ($7 all-in) by a margin that should make you ask where the money comes from. And the answer is obvious if you look at the offshore entity: 1:3000 leverage marketed to traders in Vietnam, Nigeria, and Indonesia.

The honest catch sits in that regulatory profile. One CySEC licence does not make you a Tier-1 regulated broker when four out of five entities are offshore. FSA Seychelles, FSC Mauritius, FSCA, and the newly-added FSC BVI — none of these provide investor compensation. The majority of JustMarkets clients globally sit under FSA Seychelles licence SD088, where regulatory oversight amounts to paperwork rather than active enforcement. No FCA. No ASIC. The two regulators that actually investigate complaints and shut brokers down are entirely absent here.

JustMarkets suits experienced traders who understand entity routing and want the Pro account pricing — $1 all-in per lot is remarkable value if you know how to manage your own risk. But if 1:3000 leverage sounds exciting rather than terrifying, this broker is not built for your survival.

sections.heading: Is JustMarkets Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — JustMarkets holds five licences, but the regulatory quality varies dramatically between them. The CySEC entity, JustMarkets Ltd (registration HE 361312, licence 401/21), is the only Tier-1 licence in the portfolio. It covers EU/EEA clients with ICF protection up to EUR 20,000 and enforces 1:30 leverage caps on retail forex majors. This is real regulation with real teeth.

The global entity operating under FSA Seychelles licence SD088 serves the vast majority of retail clients worldwide — anyone in Southeast Asia, Africa, the Middle East, or Latin America lands here. No compensation scheme exists. Your funds are segregated but not insured by any government body. If the entity collapses, you queue with other creditors. The FSC Mauritius licence (GB22200881) and the newly-added FSC BVI licence provide additional jurisdictional coverage but identical protection levels: zero. FSCA South Africa offers local regulatory presence but no investor compensation fund either.

Five licences looks impressive in a comparison table. But when four of five offer no compensation and limited enforcement capability, the quantity is less meaningful than it appears. JustMarkets does not appear on any Tier-1 regulatory warning list — not FCA, not ASIC, not BaFin, not IOSCO. That is genuinely positive. The broker is not flagged as fraudulent anywhere. But absence of warnings is not the same as presence of strong oversight. NAFT last reviewed JustMarkets regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: JustMarkets Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
The Pro account is where JustMarkets becomes genuinely interesting. From 0.1 pips on EUR/USD with zero commission — that is $1 all-in per standard lot. Read that again. IC Markets charges $7 all-in on cTrader. Pepperstone charges $7. FBS Standard costs $7. JustMarkets Pro costs $1. The maths is not subtle. For a trader executing 50 lots per month, that is $300 saved compared to a typical raw-spread broker. The catch? Minimum deposit is $200, and you are almost certainly on the FSA Seychelles entity with zero compensation.

The Raw Spread accounts on MT4/MT5 and cTrader offer 0.0 pip average with a $6 round-turn commission — $6 all-in, which is competitive with IC Markets cTrader pricing. Standard and Standard Cent accounts sit at 0.7 pips with zero commission ($7 all-in) — identical all-in cost to FBS Standard but with a $10 minimum deposit versus $5.

Leverage is where JustMarkets crosses from competitive to concerning. Under the offshore entities, you get up to 1:3000 on forex majors. That means a $100 deposit controls $300,000 in notional value. A 0.03% move against you wipes the account. Under CySEC, the cap is 1:30 on majors, 1:20 on minors, 1:10 on commodities — standard ESMA retail caps. The inactivity fee kicks in after 90 days of zero trading activity, which is more aggressive than IC Markets (no inactivity fee) but standard among mid-tier brokers.

sections.heading: JustMarkets Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Trustpilot data for JustMarkets is limited — not enough volume for a statistically meaningful sample. Independent community sentiment from trading forums and review aggregators is generally positive, with FXLeaders rating JustMarkets 90/99 and TradersUnion at 7.1/10 (publicly reported across multiple independent sources). The withdrawal-specific feedback pattern leans positive: crypto withdrawals processing within hours, e-wallet returns same-day, and no widespread pattern of non-payment or systematic delays.

The negative patterns that exist are worth naming. Some reports of verification delays when processing first-time withdrawals — KYC re-verification triggered for amounts over a certain threshold is standard industry practice but frustrates traders who expected instant access. The inactivity fee after 90 days has caught traders who did not read the terms, resulting in complaints that are technically the trader's fault but still represent a negative experience. No documented pattern of refused withdrawals or systematic payment failures exists in publicly available records.

If your withdrawal stalls: confirm your KYC documents are fully verified and current. Ensure you are withdrawing to the same method as your deposit for AML compliance. Contact live chat and request a specific escalation reference number. If unresolved after 3 business days, file a formal complaint through the CySEC entity complaints procedure if you are an EU client. For offshore entity clients, escalation options are more limited — this is the trade-off of offshore regulation. Document every interaction with screenshots and timestamps.

If you trade 10+ lots per month, understand that your funds sit under FSA Seychelles with zero compensation, and want the Pro account's $1 all-in pricing — JustMarkets delivers genuine value that most competitors cannot match. Set leverage to 1:30 manually, test a withdrawal before scaling past $500, and treat the regulatory protection as non-existent because it effectively is.
